# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.
I'll explore the codebase to locate the transaction-categorization enrichment logic and the fixtures behind these RC 2.14 findings.

# Transaction Categorization / Enrichment – Codebase Report

## 1. Overall project structure

**No README.** Single-commit import (`047782b`). No test suite, fixtures, baselines, or RC 2.14 references anywhere in the tree. `.gitignore` ignores `*.csv` (fixtures may have been excluded).

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # Python 3.9, gunicorn :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # Flask app package
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app bootstrap
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP API routes
        ├── BankScripts/                # Per-bank categorization (37 banks)
        └── UtilityScripts/             # Shared regex, purpose, clean names, salary, PFM
```

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | `POST /categorizeTransaction`, `/recurrentTransactions` |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` | Category + `partyName` from narration (bank-specific) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` | Bank regex patterns (cheque, verification, FT, etc.) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` | Merchant/purpose patterns (loans, P2P NBFCs, etc.) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` | DF clean + split helpers (`sep_by_`, `sep_by_dash`, `py_extract`) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` | Post-pass purpose / subcategory / merchantType |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` | Counterparty name normalization |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` | Category display labels |

**Pipeline** (per bank in `Controller.py`):

1. Bank script → `transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, `partyName`
2. `purpose()` / `card_purpose()`
3. `clean_names()` / `card_clean_names()`
4. Optional `internal_payment()`, `salary_detection()`, PFM

**Default category when nothing matches:** `"TRANSFER"` (`np.select(..., default="TRANSFER")` in every bank script).

---

## 2. Where categories and counterparty names come from

### Categories
Each bank script builds ordered `conditions_choices` and applies `np.select` on `description` / `remark` / `amount` / `type`. First match wins.

Example (HDFC):

```11:104:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
    conditions_choices = [
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^OPENING BALANCE", na=False, case=False) , "OPENING_BALANCE"],
        [transactions.description.str.contains(BANK_VER, na=False, case=False) &  transactions.amount.lt(2) , "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],
        ...
        [transactions.description.str.contains("\\b[Cc][Hh][Qq]\\b|^I/W CHQ RETURN|[Cc]heque|CHEQUE", na=False, case=False)  & transactions.type.eq("DEBIT") , "CHEQUE_PAID"],
        ...
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^UPI|UPI-?\\s?", na=False, case=False) , "UPI"],
        [transactions.description.str.contains("IMPS-", na=False, case=False) , "IMPS"],
        ...
        [(transactions.remark.str.len().eq(16)) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & transactions.remark.str.contains("^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}", na=False, case=False) , "CHEQUE_DEPOSIT"]
    ]
    ...
    transactions['transactionCategory'] = np.select(df['conditions'], df['choices'], default="TRANSFER")
```

### Counterparty (`partyName`)
Second (and often third) `np.select` pass extracts name via dash/slash/colon splits or regex. Helpers in `AppUtil.py`:

```14:18:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py
def sep_by_(description, n1, n2):
    return description.str.split('/').str[n1:n2].str.join('')

def sep_by_dash(description, n1, n2):
    return description.str.split('-').str[n1:n2].str.join('')
```

Then `CleanName.py` / bank-local cleanup rewrites junk names.

---

## 3. Test fixtures (cheques, transfers, UPI, account verification)

**None in repo.** No `tests/`, no fixtures, no baseline JSON/CSV, no pytest/unittest config.

Closest “reference” behavior is only in production bank scripts. Patterns that *should* be covered by fixtures:

| Theme | Primary files |
|-------|----------------|
| Cheques | `HDFC.py`, `PNB.py`, `Axis.py`, `Canara.py`, `BankRegexConstants.py` (`HDFC_CHQ_*`, `PNB_CHQ_*`) |
| Transfers / NEFT / RTGS / IMPS | All bank scripts + `BankRegexConstants.py` FT patterns |
| UPI / instant | `HDFC.py`, `ICICI.py`, `PNB.py`, `SBI.py`, `Canara.py`, `Kotak.py` |
| Account verification | `BANK_VER`, `BANK_VERIF`, `ACC_VERIF*`, `BANK_VER_ICICI` in `BankRegexConstants.py`; first rules in each bank script |

---

## 4. Baseline labels / RC 2.14 regression setup

**Not present.**

- No “RC 2.14”, “F-1”…“F-5”, “baseline”, or regression harness in git history or files
- `.gitignore` drops `*.csv` and `TEST*.xml`
- Labels live only as string enums in `TransactionCategoryEnums.py` (e.g. `CHEQUE_PAID="Cheque"`, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION="Account Verification"`, `UPI="UPI"`, `TRANSFER="Transfers"`)

**What would need to be added for RC 2.14:**

1. Fixture narrations for F-1…F-5 (per bank)
2. Expected `{transactionCategory, partyName, transactionSubcategory}`
3. Thin runner calling `categorize_<Bank>_transactions` (or HTTP `POST /categorizeTransaction`)
4. CI gate on those baselines

---

## 5. How tests / the service are run today

```bash
# Install
cd /app/categorizationapp && pip3 install -e .

# Run API (as Dockerfile)
gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app
# or
python -m categorizationapp   # debug on :9898

# API
POST /categorizeTransaction
# body: bank, acc_type, accountUID, accountHolder, transactions[], optional isPFMEnabled
```

**No automated tests.** Manual verification:

```python
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions
# build DataFrame with description, amount, type, remark, balanceAfterTransaction
result = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df, "SAVING")
```

Docker: `WORKDIR .../categorizationapp`, `pip3 install -e .`, expose 9898.

---

## 6. Findings F-1 … F-5 (root cause + fix)

Live reproduction with bank categorize functions confirmed the bugs below.

---

### F-1: Bare cheque number digits → TRANSFER instead of cheque

**Expected:** Description/remark that is only a cheque number (typically 5–6 digits) → `CHEQUE_PAID` / `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`.

**Actual:** Most banks fall through to default `TRANSFER`.

| Bank | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| **Axis** | Correct if `remark` matches `^[0-9]{5,6}$` |
| **PNB** | Correct if `remark` is 5–6 digits; narration like `TO TRF - 123456` alone stays `TRANSFER` |
| **HDFC** | Only 16-char zero-padded remark credits → cheque; bare `"123456"` → `TRANSFER` |
| **ICICI / SBI / Canara / Kotak** | Bare digits → `TRANSFER` |

**Working reference (Axis):**

```58:59:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Axis.py
        [transactions.remark.str.contains("^[0-9]{5,6}$", na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("DEBIT"), "CHEQUE_PAID"],
        [transactions.remark.str.contains("^[0-9]{5,6}$", na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT"), "CHEQUE_DEPOSIT"],
```

**HDFC gap:**

```100:104:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
        [(transactions.remark.str.len().eq(16)) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & transactions.remark.str.contains("^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}", na=False, case=False) , "CHEQUE_DEPOSIT"]
    ]
    ...
    transactions['transactionCategory'] = np.select(df['conditions'], df['choices'], default="TRANSFER")
```

Also, HDFC mis-labels 6-digit TRANSFER **credits** as salary subcategory:

```124:124:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
        [transactions.transactionCategory.eq("TRANSFER") & transactions.description.str.contains("^[0-9]{6}$", na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & (accountType=="SAVING") , "SALARY"],
```

**What to fix:**
1. Add (bank-wide where applicable):  
   - `description` or `remark` `^[0-9]{5,8}$` + DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`  
   - same + CREDIT → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`
2. PNB: treat `TO TRF - <chqno>` / `PNB_CHQ_0` as cheque category, not only party cleanup
3. HDFC: stop treating bare 6-digit credits as `SALARY`; classify as cheque when remark/description is cheque-like
4. Align ICICI/SBI/Canara/Kotak with Axis/PNB remark rules

---

### F-2: `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → counterparty is clearing tag, not name

**Narration split:**  
`CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → `['CHQ PAID', 'MICR CLG', 'RAVI KUMAR']`

| Bank | Category | `partyName` | Why |
|------|----------|-------------|-----|
| **Canara** | `CHEQUE_PAID` | **`Micr Clg`** | `sep_by_dash(..., 1, 2)` |
| **AU Small Finance** | `CHEQUE_PAID` | **`Micr Clg`** | same index |
| **HDFC** | `CHEQUE_PAID` | **empty** | `sep_by_dash(..., 3, 4)` OOB; then wipes `Micr Clg` |
| **Central** | `CHEQUE_PAID` | **`Ravi Kumar`** | correct `sep_by_dash(..., 2, 3)` |

**Canara (bug):**

```164:165:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Canara.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("Chq Paid-Home Clearing-", na=False, case=False), sep_by_dash(transactions.description,2,3)],
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^CHQ PAID-", na=False, case=False), sep_by_dash(transactions.description,1,2)],
```

**HDFC (wrong segment + wipe):**

```163:163:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
        [transactions.transactionCategory.isin(["TPT","UPI_REVERSAL","IMPS_REVERSAL"]) | transactions.description.str.contains("CHQ PAID-", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_dash(transactions.description,3,4)],
```

```85:86:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py
HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN5 = "Chq Paid-INWARD|CHQ PAID-INWARD| TOTAL AMT [0-9]+ CR|Chq Paid-TRANSFER|CHQ PAID-TRANSFER"
HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN6 = "Chq Paid-MICR CTS|CHQ PAID-MICR CTS"
```

`MICR CLG` is **not** in `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN6` (only `MICR CTS`). Cleanup then blanks residual tags:

```260:260:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
        [transactions.partyName.str.contains("Micr Clg|Chq Paid", na=False, case=False)  , ""],
```

**Central (correct reference):**

```74:74:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Central.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("CHQ PAID-", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_dash(transactions.description,2,3)],
```

**What to fix:**
1. Canara / AU: for `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-<NAME>` use index **2:3** (or dedicated pattern), not 1:2
2. HDFC: add `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG` pattern; extract name after last clearing tag (index 2); do not blank good names when wiping tags
3. Prefer regex like `CHQ PAID-(?:MICR\s+(?:CLG|CTS)|INWARD|TRANSFER)-(.+)` → group 1

---

### F-3: Inbound electronic transfer credits with blank counterparty

Category often correct (`NEFT`/`IMPS`/`FUND_TRANSFER`); **`partyName` empty or wrong**.

Reproduced examples:

| Bank | Narration | Category | partyName |
|------|-----------|----------|-----------|
| HDFC | `00NEFT TO SOMEONE` | NEFT | `''` |
| Canara | `IMPS- CREDIT-JOHN DOE-XX1234` | IMPS | `''` |
| SBI | `BY TRANSFER-INB IMPS/.../XX0123/JOHN DOE` | IMPS | **`Xx0123`** (mask, not name) |

**HDFC NEFT extract** expects dash-separated name after UTR; `00NEFT TO …` uses a different shape:

```157:162:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^NEFT [CD][Rr]-[A-z0-9]{11}-[0-9]{7,}-", na=False, case=False)  , sep_by_dash(transactions.description,3,4)],
        ...
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^00[0-9]+NEFT TO ", na=False, case=False) , py_extract(transactions.description, pat="NEFT TO (.*)", index=0)],
```

(`00NEFT TO` without digits between `00` and `NEFT` misses the extract.)

**Canara IMPS credit:**

```125:125:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Canara.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("IMPS- CREDIT|IMPS-CREDIT", na=False, case=False)  , sep_by_dash(transactions.description,1,2).replace(to_replace="^ CREDIT|^CREDIT", value="", regex=True)],
```

For `IMPS- CREDIT-JOHN DOE-XX1234`, segment 1 is often empty/`CREDIT`, not the name.

**SBI IMPS** picks wrong slash field (`SBI_IMPS_1/2/3` in `BankRegexConstants.py`).

**What to fix:**
1. HDFC: broaden NEFT-TO / zero-prefix patterns; map inbound credit layouts to name field
2. Canara: `IMPS- CREDIT-<NAME>-…` → `sep_by_dash(..., 2, 3)` (or extract after `CREDIT-`)
3. SBI: after IMPS split, prefer alphabetic name token over `XX####` account masks
4. Add credit-side fixtures for NEFT/IMPS/RTGS per major bank; assert non-empty human `partyName`

---

### F-4: P2P instant payment shows bare reference / tag instead of sender name

UPI is categorized, but wrong slash/dash segment becomes `partyName`.

Reproduced:

| Bank | Narration | partyName | Issue |
|------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| **PNB** | `UPI/.../CR/JOHN DOE/P2A/Payment` | **`P2A`** | Payment-type tag |
| **PNB** | `UPI/.../JOHN/P2A/pay@ybl` | **`Pay@Ybl`** | VPA, not name |
| **Canara** | `UPI/CR/<ref>/JOHN DOE/...` | **`''`** | Digit party wiped |
| **Canara** | 7-slash UPI | wrong tail field | Off-by-one segment |
| **HDFC** | `UPI-XX1234-johndoe@oksbi-…` | **`''`** | `UPI-XX` forced empty |

**PNB UPI P2A (takes index 4 → often `P2A`):**

```152:155:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/PNB.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^UPI/.*P2M/...", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_(transactions.description,4,5)],
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^UPI/.*P2M", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_(transactions.description,3,4)],
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^UPI.*P2V", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_(transactions.description,4,5)],
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^UPI.*/P2A/", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_(transactions.description,4,5)],
```

**Canara UPI + digit wipe:**

```107:109:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Canara.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^UPI/0", na=False, case=False) & transactions.description.str.count("/").eq(7) , sep_by_(transactions.description,7,8)],
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^UPI/[CD]R", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_(transactions.description,2,3)],
```

```174:174:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Canara.py
        [transactions.partyName.str.contains("\\.ifs?c?|[Pp]aytmqr|^[0-9]{5,}", na=False, case=False) , ""],
```

For `UPI/CR/<12-digit-ref>/JOHN DOE/...`, index 2 is the **reference**, then cleanup blanks it instead of falling back to the name field.

**HDFC forces empty for `UPI-XX`:**

```151:151:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^UPI-XX", na=False, case=False) , ""],
```

**What to fix:**
1. PNB P2A/P2V: extract person name (field before `P2A`/`P2V` or known name slot), reject `P2A`/`P2M`/`P2V`/`NA` as party
2. Canara: if extracted UPI party is pure digits, retry next slash segments for alphabetic name; don’t only blank
3. HDFC: for `UPI-XX…`, pull name/VPA local-part from later dash fields instead of hard `""`
4. Shared post-clean: if `partyName` ∈ `{P2A,P2M,P2V,NA,UPI}` or only digits → re-extract

---

### F-5: Account verification / “is this account live” token deposits → TRANSFER (or rail category)

Penny-drop / validation credits of ₹1 (or < ₹2) should be `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`.

**Canara bug (amount threshold):**

```19:19:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Canara.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains(BANK_VERIF, na=False, case=False) &  transactions.amount.lt(1) , "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],
```

`BANK_VERIF` includes `FUND TRANS|IMPS Txn|verif|…`, but **`amount.lt(1)` excludes ₹1**.  
Reproduced: `FUND TRANS verification` @ ₹1 → **`TRANSFER`**; @ ₹0.01 → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`.

```321:321:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py
BANK_VERIF = "verif|nydrop|valida|...|FUND TRANS|IMPS Txn"
```

**Other banks:**

| Bank | Rule | Gap |
|------|------|-----|
| HDFC | `BANK_VER` + `amount.lt(2)` | OK for keywords; uses `BANK_VER` not richer unused `BANK_VER_HD` |
| Axis | **Any** CREDIT amount ∈ `{1}` | Over-broad but catches tokens |
| SBI | keywords + CREDIT + `amount.eq(1)` | No keyword → stays TRANSFER/IMPS |
| PNB | narrow `ACC_VERIFY_PNB` | Keyword-less ₹1 IMPS stays IMPS |
| Kotak | Only `Karz Xx4002` or `^Received from [A-Z]` @ ₹1 | Plain IMPS ₹1 stays IMPS |
| Paytm | IMPS + ₹1 CREDIT → verification | Good pattern to reuse |

Unused HDFC-specific pattern (never referenced in `HDFC.py`):

```75:75:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py
BANK_VER_HD = "ACCOUNT VERIFICATION|testing|verif|pennydrop|...|/FUND TRANS/|..."
```

Purpose post-pass only flips **loan** ₹1, not general transfers:

```165:165:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py
        [transactions.transactionSubcategory.eq("LOAN") & transactions.amount.isin([1,-1]) , "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],
```

**What to fix:**
1. **Canara:** `amount.lt(1)` → `amount.le(1)` or `amount.lt(2)` / `isin([1,-1,0.01,…])`
2. Wire `BANK_VER_HD` (or expand `BANK_VER`) on HDFC
3. Cross-bank: CREDIT + amount ≤ 1–2 + (verification keywords **or** known penny-drop rails) → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` **before** generic IMPS/NEFT/UPI/TRANSFER
4. Optional Axis-like fallback: small CREDIT with empty/junk party + IMPS/NEFT → verification
5. Clear `partyName` for verification (Paytm already does)

---

## 7. Priority fix map

| Finding | Highest-impact files | Minimal change |
|---------|----------------------|----------------|
| **F-1** | `HDFC.py`, `ICICI.py`, `SBI.py`, `Canara.py`, `Kotak.py`, `PNB.py` | Axis-style 5–6 digit remark/description → cheque; fix HDFC salary collision |
| **F-2** | `Canara.py`, `AuSmallFinanceBank.py`, `HDFC.py`, `BankRegexConstants.py` | Extract name after `MICR CLG`/`MICR CTS` (index 2); extend `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN6` |
| **F-3** | `HDFC.py`, `Canara.py`, `SBI.py` (+ NEFT/IMPS credit rules) | Credit-side name patterns; reject mask tokens |
| **F-4** | `PNB.py`, `Canara.py`, `HDFC.py` | Correct UPI segment; reject `P2A`/digits-only; fallback to name |
| **F-5** | `Canara.py` (`lt(1)`), `BankRegexConstants.py`, bank ACC_VER rules, optionally `Purpose.py` | Fix threshold; expand keywords; order before rail categories |

---

## 8. Suggested regression fixtures (missing today)

```text
F-1  desc/remark "123456" DEBIT/CREDIT          → CHEQUE_PAID / CHEQUE_DEPOSIT
```

steps.reasoning_content:
Interesting findings on HDFC F-1:The issue you're seeing with HDFC F-1 is clear now: the current rule is too loose when the description is a bare digit string (or when both description and remark are digits). The regex `\b[Cc][Hh][Qq]\b` only triggers on the "CHQ" in description, but when 123456 appears alone in description (or remark), it falls through to TRANSFER.

For the Axis case you mentioned, the rule `^[0-9]{5,6}$` on remark works because it explicitly checks for a pure numeric remark. HDFC needs a similar guard: if the description/remark is purely numeric 5-6 digits and type is DEBIT, force CHEQUE_PAID.

For F-4, the PNB and Canara UPI patterns are broken because the name extraction is keyed off the wrong index after the P2A or CR separator. The name should always be the token immediately before the P2A or CR segment, not after it.

For F-3 HDFC, the regex `^00[0-9]+NEFT TO ` fails on `00NEFT TO SOMEONE` because it requires at least one digit between 00 and NEFT.
